answer: Every identity reaches the market over a bridge of its own, and the atlas counts bridges by their keystones: a new bridge must be built on the keystone of the owner's last, so a fresh purse is still the same owner to it. A bridge opens only when more fresh sponsors than its chain holds bridges lock willow rings against it; a sponsor cannot judge a twin of what it vouched for, and the atlas burns that chain's rings when one bridge proves a twin. A hundred bridges cost an operator 5,050 rings of willow and 5,050 sponsors it has never met; a newcomer costs one ring and one sponsor.
